description: Expose a project-level approval waiting time aggregation (avg/median/max over trailing 7d, keyed on respondedAt) via a new backend endpoint, and surface its average as a summary metric on the Attention Hero.

tasks.title: Backend approval-wait aggregation endpoint
tasks.description: Add `IssueQuerier.GetApprovalWaitAsync(projectId, now)` that reuses the existing `MohistDefaultWorkflowProjection` path (resolve project's WorkflowRunIds from indexed Issues, deserialize State -> WorkflowRun -> WorkflowStatusView, project each StageApproval) and aggregates avg/median/max wait in memory over completed approvals (approved/rejected, non-null RespondedAt) whose RespondedAt falls within [now-7d, now]. Expose it via `GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/issues/metrics/approval-wait` as a new `IssueRoutes.ApprovalMetrics.cs` partial mapped next to `MapIssueMetrics`, returning an `ApiResponse<ApprovalWaitMetricsResponse>` with Window, SampleCount, and nullable AverageSeconds/MedianSeconds/MaxSeconds. No new events, state collection, or writes.
acceptanceCriteria: `GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/issues/metrics/approval-wait` returns 200 with Window, SampleCount, AverageSeconds, MedianSeconds, MaxSeconds for a project that has completed approvals in the trailing 7 days.

Aggregation includes only approvals with `approvalState.status` of `approved` or `rejected` (non-null RespondedAt); approvals with `status` of `awaiting` are excluded from the denominator and never produce a wait sample.
Window is keyed on `respondedAt` in `[now - 7d, now]`; an approval responded 10 days ago is excluded while ones at 1d and 6d ago are included, and the boundary advances with the passed-in `now`.
avg/median/max are computed from the same sample set: samples [1h,2h,2h,4h,16h] yield avg 5h, median 2h, max 16h; a single 3.2h sample yields 3.2h for all three.

Zero-sample window returns a defined empty result (SampleCount == 0 with null AverageSeconds/MedianSeconds/MaxSeconds), distinguishable from a genuine zero-duration wait (SampleCount == 1, average 0).
Selection of "the approval for an issue" reuses `MohistDefaultWorkflowProjection.ProjectWorkflowState`; no second parser/selection is introduced.
Endpoint introduces no new event, state collection, or approval-domain write — it derives purely from already-populated `WorkflowRuns.State`.

`IssueQuerierSpecs` cover the aggregation: trailing-7d windowing, avg/median/max statistics, pending-approval exclusion, single-sample, and zero-sample behavior (mirroring the `GetCompletionBucketsAsync_*` test pattern with a literal `now`).
An endpoint/contract test asserts the 200 response shape for the data-present case and the zero-sample empty case.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Issue/Services/IssueQuerier.cs (new GetApprovalWaitAsync + result records), packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Api/IssueRoutes.ApprovalMetrics.cs (new partial), DTOs in Api/IssueRoutes.Dtos.cs, route mapping in IssueRoutes.cs, and passing IssueQuerier/endpoint specs.
tasks.notes: Clock seam is a passed-in `DateTimeOffset now` (parity with GetCompletionBucketsAsync), not TimeProvider. In-memory aggregation mirrors the completion precedent because EF Core SQLite cannot translate DateTimeOffset comparisons on TEXT columns. Stats are returned in seconds (not ISO duration). Route uses the literal `metrics/` prefix to avoid colliding with the `{number:int}` route.

tasks.title: Attention Hero surfaces the summary approval-wait metric
tasks.description: Add the frontend query hook `useApprovalWait()` (and `fetchApprovalWait`) in `packages/web/src/entities/issue/api/approval-wait.ts` twinning `useCompletionTrend` (query key `['issues','metrics','approval-wait',projectId]`, staleTime 60_000, enabled by !!projectId), exported via `entities/issue/index.ts`. Add `packages/web/src/shared/lib/format-duration.ts` (`formatDuration(seconds)` -> "3.2h"/"5d"/"<1m") with co-located tests. Give `AttentionHero` an optional `approvalWait?` prop and render the aggregate average wait from the aggregation (prop overrides the internal hook), plus a defined empty/zero-sample presentation (data-testid="approval-wait-empty"). Add the approval-wait query key to the approve mutation's onSuccess invalidation.
acceptanceCriteria: `useApprovalWait()` exists with query key `['issues','metrics','approval-wait',projectId]`, `staleTime: 60_000`, and `enabled: !!projectId`, and is exported through `entities/issue/index.ts`.
`formatDuration(seconds)` renders compact elapsed durations (e.g. "3.2h", "5d", "<1m") and `format-duration.test.ts` covers hour/day/minute/zero cases.

AttentionHero displays the aggregate **average** approval waiting time sourced from the approval-wait aggregation endpoint when at least one sample exists; the Hero does NOT compute the metric client-side over the full issue list.
AttentionHero accepts an optional `approvalWait?` prop that overrides the internal `useApprovalWait()` call (the unit-test seam mirroring the existing `issues?`/`agentStatus?` slots).

When the aggregation returns zero samples (SampleCount == 0 / null stats), AttentionHero renders a defined empty presentation (data-testid="approval-wait-empty", data-state="empty", muted copy) distinguishable from a genuine short wait.
The approve mutation's `onSuccess` invalidates `['issues','metrics','approval-wait']` so the metric refreshes after a human acts.
Pending (`awaiting`) approvals are excluded from the summary metric (sourced server-side) and continue to surface as individual attention items.
`AttentionHero.test.tsx` covers: metric shown from the aggregation, empty/zero-sample presentation, and the prop-override seam (using the existing hoisted-mock pattern, no MSW).
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.output: packages/web/src/entities/issue/api/approval-wait.ts (+ index.ts export), packages/web/src/shared/lib/format-duration.ts (+ .test.ts), packages/web/src/widgets/attention-hero/ui/AttentionHero.tsx, and updated AttentionHero.test.tsx — all typechecking and passing.
tasks.notes: The `completion-trend.ts` file is the exact structural twin (same folder, staleTime, key namespace, inline DTO typing). Empty presentation follows CompletionTrend's data-testid/data-state convention. No new mutations beyond the existing approve/resume actions; no client-side computation over the paginated/filtered issue list.
